title: Hokusai, Under the Wave off Kanagawa (The Great Wave)
lede: A Prussian-blue wave curls over three boats and frames a small Mount Fuji, in the most famous print of Hokusai’s Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji.
summary: Blue wave, cream sky, and a tiny Fuji in an off-center composition. Katsushika Hokusai, 1830–1833.

evidence.note: Downloaded and inspected the Art Institute of Chicago image of impression 1925.3245 (1686 × 1155 px).

styles.note: A canonical landscape print: key-block outlines, flat Prussian blue, a dark bokashi band at the horizon, a title cartouche, and an asymmetric, cropped composition.

context: AIC catalogues the sheet as a color woodblock print, ōban format, 25.4 × 37.6 cm, signed “Hokusai aratame Iitsu fude”, published by Nishimura-ya Yohachi. [AIC 1925.3245](https://www.artic.edu/artworks/24645).

AIC’s description says that the series, begun in 1830, used the newly affordable Berlin (Prussian) blue for sky and water, and that it established the popularity of landscape prints. [AIC](https://www.artic.edu/artworks/24645).
observed: A large wave rises from the left and curls toward the center. Its crest breaks into claw-like white foam outlined in thin dark lines.
The wave is printed in two flat blues, a dark Prussian blue and a pale blue, with cream paper left for the foam.
Mount Fuji is small, near the center of the lower half, framed by the trough of the wave.
The sky is a flat buff tone. A dark gray band fades upward from the horizon behind Fuji.
A narrow vertical cartouche with a thin border holds the title at upper left. The signature runs in a vertical column beside it.
Three long boats cross the lower half. A second wave at right is cut by the edge of the sheet.
The pink tones that some impressions show on the boats and sky are not visible in this copy.
interpretation: The print shows the style’s main graphic devices together: one even key line, few flat colors, a gradient used only as a band, and a cropped, asymmetric composition.
The small Fuji against the large wave is the near–far contrast that Western artists took from these prints.
borrow: Let one large shape enter from one edge and crop at another, and put the real subject small inside it.
Use two values of one blue, dark and pale, with the paper color as the third tone.

images.alt: Color woodblock print. A huge blue wave with white claw-like foam curls over three long boats. Small snow-capped Mount Fuji sits low in the trough. A vertical title cartouche is at upper left.
images.caption: Katsushika Hokusai, Under the Wave off Kanagawa, 1830/33. [Art Institute of Chicago 1925.3245](https://www.artic.edu/artworks/24645), Clarence Buckingham Collection. CC0.

rights.statement: The Art Institute of Chicago marks the object public domain (`is_public_domain: true`) and releases images of public-domain works under CC0. [AIC open access](https://www.artic.edu/open-access/open-access-images). Hokusai died in 1849, and the print was published about 1831, so the work is public domain in Japan and the United States.
